correctness.rationale: For the unit-edge path and counting norms, adjacent difference coordinates identify TV with ℓ1 on the quotient by constants, so the sharp norm is the largest step-error column norm E_k. Strict stochastic positivity fixes each error column's signs on its two sides. Telescoping the derivative of the mass on the first k sites and using D exp(−tDᵀD)=exp(−tDDᵀ)D gives E′_k(t)=2(exp(−tDDᵀ))_{kk}; the sine expansion has the stated normalization. On the 2N-cycle the odd reflection yields the diagonal h_t(0)−h_t(2k). The radial differences start at (1,0,…,0), have −3 boundary and −2 interior diagonals with +1 nearest-neighbor entries, and are strictly positive for t>0 by irreducibility (also N=2). Hence only the central cuts maximize. For two active jump coefficients with the same sign, the error columns oppose between the cuts; for opposite signs they oppose to the left of both. Thus even an odd-path tie cannot yield a maximizing mixture. Spectral differentiation, mixing and dominated convergence via the 1/r² bound verify the time behavior, derivative at zero and diffusive limit. Independent diagnostic `python /workspace/independent_replay.py 1`: 684 direct step/time versus sine-formula comparisons for 2≤N≤19, and strict loss of both signed equal-size central mixtures in odd N at those times. Rigidity for every signal and time is analytic, not asserted from this test.

value.rationale: The sharp finite-time TV control of heat approximation is a natural operator invariant, not merely a kernel computation. Its dependence on t and N and the fact that even a tied pair of central cuts admits no two-jump equality signal are useful finite-path benchmarks. The contribution is scoped away from equilibrium, continuum and the isolated N=4 case as independent novelties.
